findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment:
Observed caulking to be in a state of disrepair in the following locations:
1) The kitchen hand sink caulking was observed to be coming apart. 

Discussed with PIC, caulking will be replaced. Ensure facility is replacing caulking as needed.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Single use/single service articles are properly stored and used.
findings.comment: Observed a stack of single service bowls to be not inverted on shelf. Discussed with PIC, education was provided and bowls were inverted. Ensure any single service item is stored in a way that prevents any possible contamination.
findings.citation_text: 4-904.11(A) Kitchenware and Tableware. (A) SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and cleaned and SANITIZED UTENSILS shall be handled, displayed, and dispensed so that contamination of FOOD- and lip-contact surfaces is prevented.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment:
Observed caulking to be in a state of disrepair in the following locations:
1) The kitchen hand sink caulking was observed to be coming apart. 
2) The triple sink caulking was observed to have black mold present.
3) The mop sink caulking was observed to have black mold present.

Discussed with PIC, caulking will be replaced. Ensure facility is replacing caulking as needed.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.comment:
Observed no CFM to be on duty during inspection. Discussed with PIC. Ensure one CFM is present during all hours of operation. 

After discussion, manager on duty was able to provided proper CFM documentation. Ensure proper licensing paperwork is available in facility at all times. 

2-102.12: (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
Observed a scrub brush and 2 pads placed in the back hand washing sink. Discussed with PIC and relocated to triple sink. Ensure hand washing stations are kept accessible and are only used to wash hands. 

5-205.11: (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions.

findings.title: Utensils, equipment & linens: properly stored, dried, & handled
findings.comment:
Observed a pizza spatula and pizza knife placed in between shelving and wall behind triple sink. Discussed with PIC and relocated spatula and knife. Ensure clean utensils are stored in a way that prevents contamination. 

4-904.11: (A) cleaned and SANITIZED UTENSILS shall be handled, displayed, and dispensed to prevent FOOD- and lip-contact surface contamination. (B) UTENSILS not prewrapped shall be presented so only handles are touched by EMPLOYEES and/or CONSUMERS. (C) SINGLE-SERVCIE ARTICLES intended for FOOD- and lip-contact shall be furnished for CONSUMER with wrapper or APPROVED dispenser.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
Observed an accumulation of food debris in between the prep cooler and prep table, splash residue of pizza sauce on glass barrier, and another accumulation of food debris on the prep table near the map. Discussed with PIC, ensure non food contact surface areas are cleaned at a frequency that prevents food accumulation. 

4-602.13: NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
Observed the walk in cooler fan unit to be dripping from the pipe. Discussed with PIC. Ensure walk in cooler is repaired to prevent dripping. 

6-501.11: PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used
findings.comment:
Observed the light in the walk in cooler to be flashing on and off. Discussed with PIC. Ensure repairs are made to allow the light to function at the manufacture’s specification. 

6-303.11: The light intensity shall be at least a certain lux and present in certain areas.

findings.title: All food employees have food handler training
findings.comment:
410 ILCS 625 and IAC Section 750.3430 (C) Facility is not in compliance with the food handler law. All food handlers, other than someone who has the food service sanitation manager certificate, shall receive or obtain training in basic food handling principles as outlined in Subpart M of the Illinois Food Code. Food handlers working at a temporary food establishment are exempt from this requirement.  

(REPEAT) Observed no food handler’s licenses at the facility. Discussed with PIC. Ensure all new hires have completed food handler training within 30 days of employment. Ensure copies of the licenses are kept at the facility. License is valid for 3 years. Correct by next routine inspection.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
5-203.11: (A) Specified under LAW, facility must have a number of HANDWASHING SINKS necessary for their convenient use by EMPLOYEESS. (B) If APPROVED, automatic handwashing may be substituted. (C) IF APPROVED, chemically treated towelettes can be used. 

Observed the front hand sink of the facility to not be working per PIC. Only the rear back hand sink is operable and verified as working by the Inspector. Hand sink must be fixed to allow more convenient access to hand washing by the food preparation area. Discussed with PIC. PIC indicated the district manager is already working on fixing the sink and it should be rectified soon. Inspector will follow-up on 4/24/23. Ensure employee’s are utilizing the back hand sink before engaging in food preparation.

Food handlers working at a temporary food establishment are exempt from this requirement.  

Observed no food handler’s licenses at the facility. Discussed with PIC. Ensure all new hires have completed food handler training within 30 days of employment. Ensure copies of the licenses are kept at the facility. License is valid for 3 years. Correct by next routine inspection.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.comment:
2-102.12: (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM. 

At the time of the inspection no Certified Food Protection Manager certification is available at the facility. The store supervisor arrived during the inspection and stated that a class was being held on September 10th (tomorrow) for the facility and that he expects the certificates will be ready soon after. One of the employees at the facility (Alexis) indicated that she has the certification from when she was the GM at another store. The certification was not brought when she changed stores and still has not arrived at this time. This violation was noted on the previous routine inspection (March 8th, 2022) and the facility was given until the next routine inspection to correct the violation. No further enforcement is being included at this time.

findings.title: All food employees have food handler training
findings.comment:
410 ILCS 625 and IAC Section 750.3430 (C) Facility is not in compliance with the food handler law. All food handlers, other than someone who has the food service sanitation manager certificate, shall receive or obtain training in basic food handling principles as outlined in Subpart M of the Illinois Food Code. Food handlers working at a temporary food establishment are exempt from this requirement.  

On arrival, no Food Handler certification cards were available for inspection. PIC is aware that all employees should have food handler certifications within 30 days of hiring.

findings.title: Charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties
findings.comment:
2-102.11: Based on the RISKS inherent to the FOOD operation, PIC shall demonstrate knowledge by:  (A) Having no Priority Foundation items; (B) Being a CFM; OR (C) Responding correctly questions as they relate to the specific FOOD operation. The areas of knowledge include C1 through C16.  

Multiple Food-borne Illness Risk Factor violations noted on todays inspection. Staff training as well as PIC knowledge should be emphasized more.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.comment:
2-102.12: (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM. 

The PIC at the facility during the inspection is not a Certified Food Protection Manger. The current list of available local courses was given to the PIC and they are instructed to ensure that the PIC is a CFPM at any time that the facility is in operation.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
5-205.11: (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions. 

The hand sink next to the three part sink is observed filled with round pizza pans on inspector arrival. Inspector discussed with the the PIC and the pans were removed during the inspection to correct. PIC is instructed to ensure that all hand sinks in the facility are maintained accessible for hand washing as well as clean so as not to contaminate hands during hand washing.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
(REPEAT SITUATION) 4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria.

The sani bucket in the facility as well as the sink that the bucket pulls solution from are both observed low during the inspection (barely registering a color change = approximately 0-50ppm quat). The dispenser is not functioning at this time (and appears to have not functioned since prior to the previous routine inspection) and employees are manually making solution in the three part sink. Employees remade the solution during the inspection to correct the violation. A follow up will take place to verify that the dispenser is adequately supplying sanitizer in 2 weeks.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.comment:
2-102.12: (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM. 

No CFPM certifications are available during this inspection. PIC at the previous routine inspection stated that cards would be available but were lost in the staff movement between store. Inspector gave PIC until today to provide certifications. No certifications are available. All medium risk facilities are required to have a CFPM on site at all times of operation. PIC instructed to ensure this for the future.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria.

Sanitizer spray bottles used in the facility are observed at 0 ppm quat. Solution should be at 200 ppm to be effective. Discussion showed that the machine normally used is not useable at this time and the bottle are made manually by employees. Employees remade the solution for the bottles during the inspection to correct concentration.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-501.11: PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. 

The two hand sinks int he facility are observed pulling away from the wall, leaving a gap between the sink and the caulking. Inspector discussed with the PIC and instructed to maintain smooth, non-absorbent and easily cleanable surfaces around the hand sinks and other eras subject to moisture/ potential food debris.

findings.title: Proper hygienic practices, eating/drinking/smoking (evidence)
findings.comment:
750-530a Employees shall consume food only in designated dining areas. An employee dining area shall not be so designated if consuming food there may result in contamination of other food, equipment, utensils, or other items needing protection.

Observed 2 drinks stored on the shelves in the walk in cooler. Discussed with the person in charge (PIC) and the drinks were placed in a container during the inspection designated for employees.

findings.title: Thermometers, gauges, test kits provided
findings.comment:
750-830g A test kit shall be provided and used for checking the concentration of chemical sanitizer that measures the concentration of solution in parts per million.

The 3 part sink in the back of the facility uses a Quat based sanitizer. The facility currently only has test strips intended for CL based sanitizers. Discussed with the PIC and directed to have the correct sanitizer test strips by the next inspection.

findings.title: Premises maintained fee of litter, unnecessary articles. Cleaning and maintaining equipment properly...
findings.comment:
750-1390 Maintenance and cleaning tools such as brooms, mops, vacuum cleaners and similar equipment shall be maintained and stored in a way that does not contaminate food.

Observed a mop stored so as not to drain effectively. Directed PIC to store in a fashion so as to dry and discussed several ways to do so.

findings.title: No Certified Manager Present
findings.comment:
750-540 All Category II facilities must have at least one full-time Licensed Food Service Sanitation Manager employed at the facility to help ensure proper food handling.  Provide at least one fulltime Food Service Sanitation Manager.

Currently there is no FSSMC on record at the facility. Discussed with the PIC who stated that they were planning on taking the course in February. Will follow up in 3 months.
